questions.question: Compare the 2025 and the 2026 staff handbook. What changed for employees, point by point?

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
**Changes from the 2025 handbook to the 2026 handbook (in force 1 January 2026):**

- **Probation:** 6 → 4 months.
- **Notice after probation:** 1 → 2 months; grades G7/G8: 3 → 4 months.
- **Annual leave:** 25 → 27 days. The long-service extra of 2 days now starts after 5 years, not 8.
- **Carrying leave over:** up to 3 → 5 days; deadline 31 January → 31 March.
- **Booking long leave (over 10 days):** 4 → 6 weeks' notice.
- **Sickness certificate:** needed from the 2nd → 3rd calendar day.
- **Parental leave:** 16 → 20 weeks; full-pay weeks 12 → 16, then 60% pay.
- **Birth of a child (other parent):** special leave 2 → 5 days.
- **Site presence:** remote work previously needed the site director's written consent. Remote-capable office staff must now be on site at least 3 days a week. The Board has not decided on a different number of days; managers apply the current rule until September 2026.
- **Confidential speak-up line:** number changed.

Hours, overtime, pay review, training and leaving rules are unchanged.

gpt-6-luna.text:
The 2026 handbook applies from 1 January 2026. Changes for employees:

- **Probation:** shortened from 6 months to 4 months.
- **Notice after probation:** increased from 1 to 2 months for most employees, and from 3 to 4 months for grades G7–G8.
- **Annual leave:** increased from 25 to 27 days; the extra 2 days for service now start after 5 years, rather than 8.
- **Carryover:** increased from 3 to 5 days, with the deadline moved from 31 January to 31 March.
- **Booking longer leave:** requests for more than 10 consecutive working days now need 6 weeks’ notice, up from 4.
- **Sickness certificates:** required from the third day of absence instead of the second.
- **Parental leave:** increased from 16 weeks (12 at full pay) to 20 weeks (16 at full pay, then 60% pay).
- **Birth leave for the other parent:** increased from 2 to 5 paid days.
- **Office remote work:** eligible roles now have a minimum of 3 onsite days per week, agreed with the line manager; the 2025 handbook instead required written site-director consent for each remote-work period.
- **Speaking-up hotline:** the contact number changed.

questions.question: I'm G4 and have to go abroad for six days in October. Give me a step-by-step plan - approvals, booking, limits, money - so I don't get anything wrong.

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
I can't give you exact money figures until I know the destination and dates. Here is the plan from the policy:

1. **Request:** Raise the trip in the travel tool. Your line manager must approve it before you book. Because it is outside Verdania, the site director must also approve.
2. **Book:** Book at least 14 days before departure, or give a reason for a later booking. Flights are economy; rail is standard for journeys up to 4 hours.
3. **Hotel:** For stays starting after 1 July, the cap is €165 a night, or €210 in Verdania City and outside Verdania. Anything above the cap needs site director approval before the stay.
4. **Per diem:** You are in band B. Full days are paid at the table rate for your destination; departure and return days are paid at half. Meals provided reduce it (breakfast 20%, lunch and dinner 40% each).
5. **Advance:** Six days qualifies for a cash advance of up to €1,500.
6. **Claim:** File within 30 days of returning, with receipts for every item over €10. Late claims need Finance director approval.

Not paid: minibar, fines, private travel insurance, and costs for an accompanying person.

Tell me the destination and dates and I can give you the exact per diem and hotel figures.

gpt-6-luna.text:
1. **Before booking:** Request the trip in the travel tool and get your line manager’s approval. Because you’re travelling outside Verdania, also get the site director’s approval.
2. **Book:** Use the travel tool at least 14 days ahead; give a reason if booking later. Take rail for journeys of up to four hours by train; otherwise, flights must be economy. As G4, you can’t book business class based on grade.
3. **Stay:** For an October trip, the hotel cap is €210 per night including breakfast outside Verdania. Get site director approval before any night above the cap.
4. **Plan money:** You’re in per-diem Band B (G3–G4). The exact rate depends on your destination, which you haven’t specified. Per diem is half-rate on departure and return days; provided meals reduce it. You may request a cash advance up to €1,500 for a six-day trip.
5. **Afterward:** Claim in the expense tool within 30 days; include receipts for items over €10.

questions.question: Summarise the rules on remote work for my team - how many days, from where, what the company pays - and tell me if anything is contradictory.

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
**Days:** Remote work is allowed on up to 3 days per calendar week, so staff are on site at least 2 days. Each team fixes one common site day. Only employees whose tasks don't need them at a machine, counter or lab qualify, after probation and with line manager agreement.

**Where:** Work from the home address registered with People. Other addresses in Verdania are allowed for up to 10 working days a year. Work from abroad is allowed for up to 20 working days a year, only from People-approved countries, and must be approved at least 4 weeks ahead.

**Company pays:** Halden Works provides a laptop, headset and one screen. A €30 monthly allowance goes to staff who work remotely at least 8 days in the month. Furniture is not paid for.

**Contradiction:** The Staff Handbook 2026 says office staff whose role allows remote work must be on site at least 3 days a week. The remote work policy says at least 2. The documents don't say which one prevails.

questions.question: Write an overview for a new G3 technician at Arden - probation, notice, leave, pension, meals, training, pay day.

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
**Overview for a new G3 technician at Arden (2026 rules)**

- **Probation:** 4 months from your first working day. Your line manager reviews you at the end of month two and two weeks before the period ends. Either side can end the contract with 2 weeks' notice.
- **Notice after probation:** 2 months to the end of a calendar month, for both you and Halden Works.
- **Leave:** 27 paid working days per year. Requests are made in the People portal. Leave of more than 10 consecutive working days needs 6 weeks' notice.
- **Pension:** The company pays 6% of gross salary. You pay at least 3%, and each extra percent up to 2 more is matched at half a percent. Membership starts after probation.
- **Meals:** Arden has no canteen, so you receive a €9.50 meal voucher for each working day.
- **Training:** 5 paid training days and a €1,200 budget per year. Book at least 3 weeks ahead.
- **Pay day:** Salary is paid on the 27th of each month, or the working day before. Your payslip appears in the People portal three working days before pay day.

questions.question: Compare the DD-1840 and the DD-1860 for me - torque, weight, protection, price - and tell me which one makes sense for fitting kitchens.

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
The DD-1840 and DD-1860 compare as follows:

- **Torque:** DD-1840 is 105 Nm. DD-1860 is listed at 140 Nm, but service bulletin SB-2026-03 corrects this to 130 Nm.
- **Weight (without battery):** DD-1840 is 1.5 kg. DD-1860 is 1.7 kg.
- **Protection:** DD-1840 is IP54. DD-1860 is IP56.
- **Price (2026 list, incl. VAT):** DD-1840 is €219. DD-1860 is €289.

The documents do not mention kitchens. The DD-1840 is described as "made for fitting out and interior work," which suits kitchen fitting better than the DD-1860, which is "made for plumbing and heating." It is also lighter and cheaper. The DD-1860 has more torque and better dust and water protection, which matter less for interior fitting.

questions.question: The dealer handbook says 2 years for professional tools, the warranty terms say 3. Which is right and why, and what must the customer do and avoid to keep the warranty?

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
The warranty terms are right: **3 years** for professional tools, if registered. The Warranty Terms 2026 state that they prevail over the catalogue, the dealer handbook and any leaflet. The handbook's 2-year figure is out of date for this purpose.

To keep the warranty, the customer must register the tool on the Orrin website within 30 days of purchase, with the serial number and receipt. An unregistered professional tool gets only 1 year.

**HX-50 maintenance plan (what / how often / who):**
- Air-side heat exchanger clean and fin check: every 3 months if dusty, otherwise yearly (operator or technician)
- Strainer: 4 weeks after commissioning, then yearly (technician)
- Refrigerant leak test: every 6 months, because the HX-50 charge is 8.9 kg, above the 5.0 kg threshold (certified technician)
- Compressor oil level and acidity: every 12 months (certified technician)
- Electrical terminals and thermal scan, safety chain test, water quality: yearly (technician; the safety chain test needs a certified technician)
- Hot water tank anode: every 24 months (technician)
- Condensate drain and heater: before each winter (operator or technician)
- Firmware: check yearly (technician)

questions.question: Our HX-35 keeps showing F212 on cold mornings. Explain why that happens, what the unit does about it, and what has to be changed.

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
**Why it happens:** F212 means the defrost cycle ended on its time limit because there was not enough energy in the water circuit. In frost, the unit defrosts itself, and it draws that energy from the water. If the buffer tank is too small, the defrost cannot finish in time.

**What the unit does:** It logs a warning. After three in a row, it switches to backup heating.

**What to change:** The buffer tank must hold at least 300 litres for the HX-35. Also check the water flow, which must not drop below the HX-35's minimum of 4.5 m³/h. The strainer should be clean, since a low flow is the most common cause of these faults in the first week.

questions.question: When do I need glycol in an HX system, how much, and what does it cost me in performance?

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
**Glycol is needed** when the water circuit runs outdoors without frost protection by other means. Use a propylene glycol mix.

**Amount:** The manual gives two shares. 25% protects to -10 °C, and 35% protects to -17 °C. Never use ethylene glycol or a mix above 40%.

**Performance cost:**
- At 25%: capacity drops 4%, required flow rises 6%, and pump head needed rises 12%.
- At 35%: capacity drops 7%, required flow rises 11%, and pump head needed rises 20%.

The documents do not give a price for the glycol itself.

questions.question: List everything the installation manual requires on the water side before the unit is connected and filled.

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
Before connecting and filling the water side, the installation manual requires:

1. Flush the system before connecting the unit.
2. Fit the supplied strainer in the return, with shut-off valves on both sides.
3. Fit flexible connections of at least 500 mm.
4. Fill with water of pH 8.2 to 10.0 and hardness of at most 8.4 degrees dH. Harder water must be softened.
5. Pressure test the circuit at 4.5 bar for 2 hours.
6. Set the cold system pressure to 1.5 bar.
7. Provide a buffer tank holding at least the volume given in section 2 of the manual. Without it, fault F212 appears in frost.

If the water circuit runs outdoors without other frost protection, use a propylene glycol mix of 25% or 35%. Never use ethylene glycol or a mix above 40%.

questions.question: This unit runs firmware 3.0. What is the default of P112?

claude-haiku-5-5.text:
On firmware 3.0, the default for P112 (anti-legionella target temperature) is **60 °C**. On 2.4 it was 55 °C. The change was made because the backup heater is not needed up to 60 °C.

Updating to 3.0 keeps any value the installer has already set. Only parameters still at the old default move to the new one. So if your unit was on 55 °C before the update, it will now read 60 °C. If someone had set a custom value, that value stays.
